sn8.9:1.2: Koṇḍañña gained his nickname as he was the first person to realize the Dhamma after the Buddha ([sn56.11:14.3]()). His absence was due to his love of solitude, as expressed in his verses ([thag15.1:0.4]()). Due to this, he features rarely in the early texts, but the Buddha once saw him meditating ([ud7.6]()), and praised him as the senior mendicant ([an1.188:1.1]()).
sn8.9:3.1: Used more generally of early disciples at [sn16.5:5.3]().
sn8.9:3.4: Not the three consisting of body, mind, and attachments, for this is only found in later texts ([mnd2:11.2]()). Perhaps the three consisting of ethics, view, and ending of defilements ([an3.93:5.1]()). But since the absorptions are often called “blissful meditations” ([sn21.4:3.3]()) and “seclusion” ([mn64:9.2]()), it’s more satisfying to read the two phrases together.
